overview: White gains space with d5 and Black plays ...e6 and ...exd5 or ...g6 and ...d6 to reach a Modern Benoni structure. White usually plays Nc3, e4 and Nf3 for a central majority; Black counters with queenside play (...b5, ...a6) and pressure on the e-file. The game is an unbalanced space-against-counterplay fight.

white_ideas.idea: Nc3, e4, Nf3 and a centre pawn majority supported by the d5 wedge
Play on the e-file and e5 or f4 breaks

black_ideas.idea: ...e6 and ...exd5 to open the e-file, ...d6, ...g6 and ...Bg7
Queenside expansion with ...a6 and ...b5, hitting c4

typical_structures.structure: Modern Benoni: White d5/e4 against Black pawns d6/c5/g6 with a queenside pawn majority

character.notes: Imbalanced Benoni: Black accepts a weak d6 for active pieces; sharp lines with ...Nxe4 and e5 pushes.

gambit.notes: No gambit; the Benko is a different line.

structure.notes: Fixed asymmetrical centre with d5 wedge; play along the e- and c-files, semi-open.

approach.notes: Played by strong players, not universally; entering via the Old Benoni transposes.

level.notes: Needs known theory and good understanding of the pawn breaks.

sublines_that_differ.name: Old Benoni 3.Nc3 and quiet lines
sublines_that_differ.how: More restrained set-ups where White avoids the Modern Benoni main lines.

character.reason: Imbalanced structure with tactical breaks; some quieter branches.

structure.reason: Fixed asymmetric centre pressed along files.

approach.reason: Played by strong players now and then.

level.reason: Demands theory and good feel for pawn breaks.

plans.reason: White's d5 wedge against Black's queenside majority.
